Ransomware Attack Disrupts Kyrgyz Metals & Mining Firms

A coordinated ransomware attack has struck several leading metals and mining firms in Kyrgyzstan, causing widespread disruption in the industry and raising concerns about the sector’s cyber resilience. The assault, which began late Tuesday, has forced multiple companies to halt or curtail operations as their IT systems remain compromised.

Among those affected are Kyrgyz Metals Processing and Ala-Too Mining, both of which confirmed on Wednesday that production at major sites has been temporarily suspended. "Our primary data servers have been encrypted, and key operational systems are offline," said Adilet Sadykov, spokesperson for Kyrgyz Metals Processing. "We are working with authorities and cybersecurity experts to restore our networks, but at this stage we cannot estimate when full operations will resume."

The attack reportedly involves a ransomware variant that demands payment in cryptocurrency to unlock critical data. The State Committee for Industry and Energy issued a statement urging all sector firms to enhance their cyber defenses and report any suspicious network activity. "This incident highlights the urgent need for robust cybersecurity protocols across the metals and mining sector," the committee said.

Initial estimates from the Kyrgyz Mining Association suggest that daily losses from suspended activities could exceed $1.5 million, with potential impacts on export contracts if the disruption continues. "This is a stark reminder that the digital infrastructure of our industry is as vital as our physical assets," noted Talgat Omuraliev, president of the association.

Some union representatives have expressed concern about the possible impact on wages if the outage is prolonged. "A halt in production means uncertainty for our members," said Ainura Mamatova, head of the mining workers’ union. "We are urging companies to prioritize employee support during this period."

As of Wednesday evening, IT teams at affected companies continue to assess the extent of the breach and work to contain the fallout. The government has not confirmed whether the attackers have been identified. Authorities are urging all industry players to remain vigilant as the situation develops.
